title: Calibration executor fanout and run snapshot access matrix
creator: Asha Raman
description: Problem: Calibration runs produce large multi-file artifacts (KV cache snapshots, traces, quant profiles, accuracy reports). Operators need deterministic, auditable snapshots for regression validation and rollback, and product teams need a clear access matrix so that multi-tenant teams can share or pin snapshots without exposing raw customer data. Goal: Implement executor-level fanout and deterministic run snapshotting in the Console with an access matrix that supports pin/read/run/audit roles, immutability for pinned snapshots, and a retention/GC model that balances reproducibility with storage cost.
acceptance_criteria: Executor can fan out calibration campaigns across configurable worker shards and emit per-shard snapshot checkpoints
Each calibration run produces a content-addressed snapshot manifest that lists artifacts and deterministic seeds
Console UI exposes a snapshot selector for pin/clone/restore and shows snapshot immutability/size/age
RBAC: roles owner/runner/viewer/auditor enforced via org groups; cross-tenant access blocked by default
API: createSnapshot(), listSnapshots(), getSnapshotManifest(), restoreSnapshot() endpoints implemented and documented
Audit: every snapshot create/modify/read/restore action is logged to the audit stream with run and user identity
Retention: default TTL applied and GC removes non-pinned snapshots after TTL; pinned snapshots require explicit owner release
Automated accuracy validation runs can attach their pass/fail status to snapshot metadata
run_spec: Fanout model: controller shards work by parameter sweep ranges (seed, calibration-batch, per-channel thresholds). Each worker writes a local checkpoint and then an atomic snapshot upload to the artifact store. Checkpoints include deterministic RNG seed, model hash, tokenizer hash, input-sample-hash, and metric snapshots. Fanout supports optimistic-concurrency merges for combined snapshot manifests.
retention_policy: Default non-pinned snapshots: 90 days TTL then GC. Pinned snapshots: retained 365 days and require manual unpin to GC (owner override only). Emergency retention: customer-impacting runs can be escalated to indefinite retention via support workflow. Storage cost estimate: average snapshot 120MB, expected additional storage at full scale ~3TB/month for default retention.
permission_matrix: Roles: owner (full), runner (create snapshots, run/restore), viewer (read-only access to snapshot metadata and read artifacts if granted), auditor (read audit logs, read-only snapshots with obfuscated inputs). Mapping: SSO groups map to RBAC roles. Cross-tenant isolation: snapshot manifests are namespaced by org-id; shared snapshots require explicit share ACL entry. KMS-protected artifacts require org-level KMS key access to read.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary UI): expose snapshot selector and read-only manifests to a small set of internal teams (2 teams)
Phase 2 (executor + API): enable fanout and snapshot creation in sandbox projects; collect perf and storage metrics
Phase 3 (RBAC + retention): enforce permission matrix and TTL GC in all staging orgs; security review and penetration test
Phase 4 (gradual beta): opt-in for customer orgs, monitor errors and storage costs for 2 weeks
Phase 5 (GA): rollout to all orgs with default retention, add billing line-item for snapshot storage
QA_plan: End-to-end tests: create a multi-shard calibration campaign, verify snapshot manifests and artifacts are reproducible
Permission tests: validate owner/runner/viewer/auditor behaviors across orgs and shared snapshots
Storage/GC tests: simulate TTL expiry and GC runs in a staging environment
Load tests: fanout 1k concurrent worker shards to observe controller throttling and cost
Security tests: KMS access gating, audit log tamper-resistance checks
